quarterly_data.quarter: DENSO results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: DENSO Q1 FY2027 results briefing (company's summary of Q&A): the sharp rise in Q1 parts costs came mainly from higher prices of raw materials such as copper, aluminum and platinum and of parts including semiconductor memory; rising material costs were in the initial plan, but market prices rose further than anticipated. For the full year the company raised only its revenue forecast, reflecting the favorable foreign-exchange effect of a weaker yen realised in Q1 and volume effects, and left operating profit unchanged because highly uncertain risks such as the Middle East situation and rising material costs were already planned for at the start of the year and recent changes can be absorbed within those assumptions. It expects no significant difference in the full-year North American tariff impact between FY2026 and FY2027, having advanced localization across North America including Mexico and Canada with customers, and expects tariff costs to stay within its plan.

quarterly_data.quarter: DENSO results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2027 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Kumamoto earthquake (DENSO Q1 FY2027 results briefing Q&A summary): DENSO's three Kyushu manufacturing sites (MORTEC, DENSO Kyushu and DENSO Miyazaki) had no impact on production and no injuries, and all facilities operate normally; some Toyota Group companies have facilities closer to the epicenter. Of about 30 suppliers being assessed, as of July 31, 2026, 16 were confirmed unaffected, 13 were still under assessment and 1 was affected; the company could not yet quantify any impact on production or results.
